content: The Spotted Jelly, scientifically known as Mastigias papua or commonly referred to as the Lagoon Jelly, is a species of jellyfish. This organism predominantly inhabits the waters of the South Pacific region. Unlike many other jellyfish species that possess a single central mouth, the Spotted Jelly exhibits multiple smaller mouth openings located on its oral arms. These openings facilitate feeding, primarily on zooplankton. In Japan, particularly along the Pacific coastal areas, Spotted Jellies are commercially sold as novelty pets. They are often marketed alongside photoautotrophic phytoplankton and are locally referred to as takokurage (タコクラゲ), which translates to octopod or rammer jellies. These jellyfish have a relatively short lifespan, averaging around four months, and are most active during the mid-summer to early fall seasons.
